correctness.rationale: For Haar-uniform z on the two-torus, t_j=v_j dot z with v_j=(A^T)^j e1, A=[[2,1],[1,1]], v_{j+2}=3v_{j+1}-v_j. Distinct vectors v_i,v_j are linearly independent so their torus phases are pairwise independent. The proof considers signed Fourier zero relations of length <=5; after cancelling pairs a one-vs-many relation is impossible by positivity and Cauchy--Schwarz of lambda^j and lambda^-j, and a 2-vs-2 relation forces equal multisets. The 2-vs-3 equation in Lucas sequence L_h−1=L_p+L_q+L_(p+q) isolates h=2,p=q=0 and v_j−3v_(j+1)+v_(j+2)=0. I independently enumerated all signed length<=5 integer frequency relations among sixteen consecutive v_j with repeated times: no new relation at degrees 1..4 and only 14 consecutive shifted five-term types, each with two sign choices. Exact Fourier coefficients yield E[X_j X_(j+1)^3 X_(j+2)]=sin(alpha)/16 and E[S_N^5]=5/4 (N−2)_+ sin(alpha), with lower moments and cumulants from cancellations. These finite checks corroborate; all-time classification depends on the analytic Lucas inequality, not enumeration.
